chose: No v0.10.0 tag: backfill six tags (v0.10.1, v0.10.2, v0.11.0, v0.11.1, v0.11.2, v0.12.0), not the seven requested
over: Tagging some commit as v0.10.0 to complete the requested sequence
Tagging 0002271 as v0.10.0 because it is the first post-0.9.0 release commit
because: package.json at every commit reachable from any ref never held 0.10.0: 'git log --all -S"version": "0.10.0"' returns EMPTY, and 0002271 bumps 0.9.0 -> 0.10.1 in one hop. 0.10.0 was never released, so no commit can honestly carry that tag. Inventing one would fabricate a release and make bisect worse, not better -- the stated purpose of the backfill. Note 0002271's own body says features are off by default so a project 'parses and grades exactly as it did in 0.10.0', a self-reference to a version that never shipped.

chose: Tag each version at the commit that DECLARED it (the package.json bump), so v0.10.1 -> 0002271
over: Tagging v0.10.1 at b012a54, the LAST commit still carrying version 0.10.1
Tagging v0.10.1 at 09b7c40 so the tag includes the parse-site bugfix
because: Three commits carry version 0.10.1: 0002271 (bump+release), 09b7c40 (fix), b012a54 (docs). Tagging the bump matches all 19 existing tags in this repo -- v0.9.0 points at the merge that released it while THREE later commits still read 0.9.0 -- and matches 09b7c40's own subject 'fix(0.10.1):', which declares itself a patch ON TOP of an already-released 0.10.1. It is also strictly better for bisect: the kind-strip bug is introduced in 0002271 and fixed in 09b7c40, so under this rule the bug lives in the range v0.10.1..v0.10.2 and is FINDABLE; tagging the last-at-version would bury both inside v0.10.1 where bisect can never see it.

chose: Commit RELEASE-NOTES.md on main, switching off the checked-out branch scene-promise-panel to do it
over: Committing on scene-promise-panel, the branch that was actually checked out
Leaving the notes uncommitted and reporting the ambiguity
because: The brief asserted 'main = origin/main = 0e87378' but the checked-out branch was scene-promise-panel, which points at the SAME commit and has no unique work (its content merged at 04712de). Release notes for shipped releases belong on the release branch, and main is the branch the task named. Because the two refs are identical the checkout changes zero files. Nothing is pushed: the task says do not push a branch, so main ends one commit ahead of origin/main, unpushed, for the user to review.

chose: Report the untagged v0.5.2 rather than tag it
over: Also backfilling v0.5.2 at 57353cf since it is the same class of defect
because: 57353cf carries package.json 0.5.2 and has no tag, so the tag history has a SECOND hole outside the range the task enumerated. Tagging it is a one-line fix, but the task scoped the backfill to v0.10.x-v0.12.0 and this is pre-v0.9.0 history; adding tags nobody asked for to old releases is scope creep on published history. Surfaced as a recommendation instead: 'git tag -a v0.5.2 57353cf'.

chose: Write my decision journal into the coherence repo, not planetizer where the hook minted the session
over: Logging to planetizer/.coherence/decisions/, the repo whose SubagentStart hook minted s-eca025c83915
Skipping the journal entirely because the two repos disagree about where it belongs
because: My agent cwd was planetizer and the hook minted the session there, but the WORK was entirely in coherence, and the task forbade touching planetizer (another stream mid-edit). CONSEQUENCE A FUTURE AGENT NEEDS: coherence's .gitignore lists '.coherence/', so these entries live at .coherence/decisions/s-eca025c83915.jsonl and are LOCAL-ONLY -- a fresh clone of coherence has no journal at all, and 'coherence decisions' there will read empty forever. The tool does not track its own decision journal. Planetizer by contrast tracks .coherence/decisions/*.jsonl. If the next release agent wants this reasoning to survive, that ignore rule is the thing to change.

chose: Commit RELEASE-NOTES.md directly on main, overriding my standing 'if on the default branch, branch first' default
over: Creating a docs branch for the release notes per the branch-first default
because: My operating guidance says to branch before committing on the default branch. Overrode it because the task explicitly scoped the work to main AND forbade pushing a branch -- so a side branch would have left main without the notes and produced a ref nobody asked for and nothing could push. The commit is local and unpushed (main ahead of origin/main by 1, bb1a620), so it is fully reversible with 'git reset --hard origin/main'. Recording it because a reviewer seeing main ahead-by-one should know it was deliberate, not drift, and should know the undo.

chose: Leave the orphaned hook-opened session header sitting in planetizer rather than reconcile the split session
over: Copying my 6 coherence entries into planetizer/.coherence/decisions/s-eca025c83915.jsonl to reunite the session
Deleting the orphaned planetizer header so the split leaves no misleading trace
because: MEASURED, and it refines d-79110bfb which I filed without knowing this: session s-eca025c83915 is SPLIT ACROSS TWO REPOS. planetizer/.coherence/decisions/s-eca025c83915.jsonl exists with exactly 1 line -- the header openSession() wrote at SubagentStart, before I ran anything -- while all 6 of my decisions are in coherence. So 'coherence decisions --session s-eca025c83915' run in planetizer shows a hook-opened session with ZERO decisions, which reads as an agent that decided nothing. That is the exact inverse of the tell v0.11.1 was built on (entries but no hook-opened sessions); nobody is watching for hook-opened sessions with no entries. Left as-is because both fixes require WRITING to planetizer, which the task forbade. Corroborating detail: the SubagentStop hook reported '68 entries' both before and after I logged 2 more, because it counts planetizer's journal, not the one I was writing to.
